terms.definition: Carbon dioxide, water vapour and methane: they absorb long-wavelength (infrared) radiation re-emitted by the Earth and keep it warm.
terms.examiner: Short-wavelength radiation from the Sun passes through.

terms.definition: Burning fossil fuels and deforestation increase carbon dioxide.
terms.examiner: Methane increases from cattle farming and rice fields.

terms.definition: Changes to the climate caused by rising global temperature: sea level rise, extreme weather, changes in food production and species distribution.
terms.examiner: Peer-reviewed evidence supports the link to human activity.

terms.definition: The total amount of carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases emitted over the full life cycle of a product, service or event.
terms.examiner: Reduced by renewables, energy efficiency, carbon capture and taxes.
